checks.finding: design.md:1256-1258 (SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate) states AC-006's per-case ownership is established because 'the Automated/Manual Classification Table above assigns to T-005's exclusive scope.' The Automated / Manual Classification Table it cites (design.md:1294-1328, 'Automated / Manual Classification Table (REQ-006; AC-025)') has exactly four columns (Check (AC) | Current Classification | Upgrade Condition | Gating fact/reason) and never names T-005, T-001, or any task ID in any of its 15 rows. The decision that governs when AC-006's SKIP becomes a hard failure (clause (a) of the Activation predicate) rests on a citation to an artifact section that does not contain the claimed content. Separately, the same section's ownership statement for AC-015/AC-016 -- 'activate with the tasks that seed their own allowlist entries (T-008 onward)' -- names an open-ended range rather than a determinate owner, unlike AC-006's (falsely cited but at least singular) T-005 assignment; 'onward' does not identify which specific task's start is the actual trigger. Concrete failure mode: a Phase 2/3 implementer or reviewer cannot verify the AC-006 ownership claim against its cited source, and cannot determine a concrete activation trigger for AC-015/AC-016 at all from design.md alone -- both are load-bearing facts for whether an Epic-A1-dependent SKIP correctly converts to a hard failure.

design.md's '## Open Questions' section (lines 1523-1536) carries OQ-001 and OQ-002 (both carried forward from requirements.md) without the literal 'Blocks Implementation:'/'Resolution Path:' field labels this check's rubric names, but each entry substantively identifies a deferral owner (Phase 2/3 implementer) and a concrete resolution mechanism -- OQ-001: empirical headless-contract confirmation feeding the existing Classification Table's automated/manual fallback with no further design change needed either way; OQ-002: already marked resolved, citing the Coverage Scope table as the single normative statement -- and neither blocks this Phase 1 package's own deliverable (a specification, not code). Per the check's own carve-out for non-blocking entries with a stated owner, this is at most a Minor formatting advisory, not a Major finding.

design.md's Assumptions section (lines 1516-1521) delegates to requirements.md's own Assumptions section (lines 718-742), each of whose four entries cites a specific grounding fact (Epic A1/A5/A7 unmerged status; ADR-0019/decision-doc as unrevised authoritative source; .gitattributes/installer/hook-config files as stable cross-runtime surfaces, cross-referenced to INV-numbers). investigation.md is present in the feature directory (confirmed by directory listing, though it is outside this reviewer's allowed_input_manifest and was not read), so the 'investigation.md absent' trigger for this check does not apply. No assumption in this section is an ungrounded free assertion.

requirements.md AC-006 (lines 283-287) states the canary case is 'Named SKIP (citing Epic A1's tracking issue) until Epic A1 merges,' and requirements.md's Main Workflows item 7 (lines 665-670) states 'As Epic A1 merges, a follow-up task un-skips AC-006/AC-015/AC-016 ... and exercises all five of A1's migrated consumer entry points per runtime' -- both frame Epic A1 merging as the operative trigger for ending SKIP status. design.md's revised SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate (lines 1245-1274) instead makes activation (the point a still-present SKIP becomes a hard failure) require BOTH the owning task starting AND the artifacts existing on main -- so AC-006's SKIP can remain non-failing for an unbounded period after Epic A1 actually merges, contingent solely on when T-005 (or, for AC-015/AC-016, an unspecified task in the open-ended 'T-008 onward' range) happens to start. This is the exact scenario security-spec.md's own B3 STRIDE threat row (line 74) names as the risk to close: 'A SKIP survives unnoticed after Epic A1 merges because nothing ever re-checks whether the cited dependency has actually landed ... permanently masking a coverage gap.' The revised gate reintroduces a structurally identical failure mode through a different mechanism (task-start gating instead of missing re-checks), and neither design.md's SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate section nor its Risks section (lines 1538-1546, which only carries forward requirements.md's original Risks) names this new failure mode or any bound/safeguard against it. design.md's stated rationale for clause (a) justifies fixing the AC-006/T-001 Done-When conflict but never acknowledges or defends the specific, functionally different consequence that AC-006/AC-015/AC-016 can now stay non-failing indefinitely past 'Epic A1 merges,' contradicting the plain reading of requirements.md AC-006 and Workflow item 7. Concrete failure mode: if the owning task is deprioritized or blocked after Epic A1 merges, AC-028's ADR-0019 delegation-discharge Done/release gate can be silently deferred indefinitely with no design-specified detection mechanism, undermining the 'never an unexplained or indefinitely-extended SKIP' intent security-spec.md itself states for boundary B3.
No performance requirements found in requirements.md. No numeric thresholds, SLA statements, or response-time/throughput/concurrency/latency language present.

High-risk surfaces present: B1 live-host session authenticity, B4 nonce/signing forgery-resistance, B5 classification-mismatch/synthetic-substitution, and cross-service (three-CLI) integration failure behavior. Each names a concrete validation path: security-spec.md's Security Tests table (lines 199-209) cites specific Test Strategy items (5, 7, 8, 10) and the validate-live-host-proof aggregate check with named non-zero-exit error codes (ERR_NONCE_REUSED, ERR_SIGNATURE_INVALID, ERR_SYNTHETIC_SUBSTITUTION, ERR_STALE_SKIP) as concrete, inspectable acceptance criteria. The one gap identified in this review -- the SKIP Allowlist Activation Gate's task-start-gated indefinite-extension risk against boundary B3 -- is recorded once under NO-REQ-CONTRADICTION rather than duplicated here, per the calibration's Finding Evidence Gate de-duplication rule (item 4); that gap is the missing concrete validation/monitoring path for B3's own stated threat model (security-spec.md line 74) and should be read as supporting evidence for that finding, not a second Major.
